# prism-cli command reference

<!-- Generated by cli/scripts/gen-cli-reference.mjs from the CLI's --help output. Do not edit by hand: run `npm run docs` in cli/ and commit the result. -->

Every command and option of prism-cli 1.12.1, exactly as `--help` prints it. For what each feature does and how to set it up, follow the **Guide** link under each command, or start at [Using PRISM locally](../USER_GUIDE.md#using-prism-locally). What each command touches in AWS is in the [prism-cli Overview](PRISM-CLI-OVERVIEW.md).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`prism-cli dashboard`](#prism-cli-dashboard) | Local web dashboard (127.0.0.1 only): codewatch results, codeburn usage, and a Setup page that runs local setup steps. Read-only in AWS. |
| [`prism-cli mcp`](#prism-cli-mcp) | MCP server on stdio for Kiro, Claude Code and other MCP clients: read-only codewatch findings and reports, cached spend and the setup checklist, a static dashboard snapshot file, the live dashboard on 127.0.0.1 as a child process, and prism_review, which runs the harness review now and writes its result file. The MCP server itself opens no port; it exits when stdin closes, stopping that dashboard. |
| [`prism-cli statusline`](#prism-cli-statusline) | Claude Code status line: reads Claude Code's status JSON on stdin and prints the latest codewatch review counts, spend today and this month, and the session's cost, lines, context and cache. Reads cached files only; set it up with prism-cli enable claude-code. |
| [`prism-cli version`](#prism-cli-version) | Print the CLI version, check npm for a newer release, and warn about other prism-cli copies on PATH |
| [`prism-cli assessment`](#prism-cli-assessment) | Run the PRISM D1 Velocity assessment: scan a repo, or run or deploy the assessment web app |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli assessment deploy-cdk`](#prism-cli-assessment-deploy-cdk) | Deploy the assessment web app to AWS via CDK (ECS + Cognito + ALB) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli assessment interview-agent`](#prism-cli-assessment-interview-agent) | interview-agent |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli assessment run`](#prism-cli-assessment-run) | Run the PRISM D1 Velocity scanner against a repository |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli assessment web`](#prism-cli-assessment-web) | Launch the assessment web interface |
| [`prism-cli aws`](#prism-cli-aws) | Connect an AWS profile, run read-only account checks and turn them into a fix list |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli aws check`](#prism-cli-aws-check) | Read-only AWS account checks: Bedrock protection, PRISM setup, account baseline (results saved for aws recommend and the dashboard) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli aws connect`](#prism-cli-aws-connect) | Choose and verify the AWS profile and region the other AWS commands default to (read-only; stores no credentials) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli aws recommend`](#prism-cli-aws-recommend) | Turn the latest aws check result into a ranked fix list (no AWS calls; --refresh runs aws check first) |
| [`prism-cli bedrock-protection`](#prism-cli-bedrock-protection) | Audit an AWS account, organization or repo for LLMjacking exposure |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-account`](#prism-cli-bedrock-protection-scan-account) | Audit the AWS account for LLMjacking exposure: IAM credential hygiene plus Bedrock spend guardrails, detection speed and invocation logging |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-org`](#prism-cli-bedrock-protection-scan-org) | Audit an AWS Organization or specific OUs: per-account IAM credential hygiene plus org-wide Bedrock spend guardrails |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-repo`](#prism-cli-bedrock-protection-scan-repo) | Scan a git repository for credentials with gitleaks: full history across all refs, working tree, commit messages, and ignore-file hygiene |
| [`prism-cli bootstrapper`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper) | Install PRISM CI workflows, the eval harness and the coding agent, and set up CI OIDC roles |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper install-coding-agent`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-install-coding-agent) | Install the PRISM coding agent (issue → fix → PR) into the current repo |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper install-eval-harness`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-install-eval-harness) | Install the kiro-cli eval gate (review rules + workflow + secret scanning) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper install-git-hooks`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-install-git-hooks) | [deprecated] Alias for "prism-cli enable codewatch" (the prepare-commit-msg trailer hook is retired) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper install-github-workflows`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-install-github-workflows) | Install GitHub Actions workflow templates into the current repo |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper install-gitlab-workflows`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-install-gitlab-workflows) | Install GitLab CI workflow templates into the current repo |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper setup-github-oidc`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-setup-github-oidc) | Set up GitHub OIDC identity provider and IAM role for GitHub Actions |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper setup-gitlab-oidc`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-setup-gitlab-oidc) | Set up GitLab OIDC identity provider and IAM role for GitLab CI/CD |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli bootstrapper setup-otel-sync`](#prism-cli-bootstrapper-setup-otel-sync) | [deprecated] Alias for "prism-cli enable codeburn" |
| [`prism-cli codewatch`](#prism-cli-codewatch) | Git hook entry points and scan reports for the local codewatch hooks, and the agent harness loop (review, hook) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli codewatch hook`](#prism-cli-codewatch-hook) | Agent harness loop hook adapter: reads a coding client's hook JSON on stdin and prints its decision. Clients: claude, kiro. Events: claude session-start, pre-tool, post-tool, stop, pre-push, bash-guard, session-end; kiro session-start, pre-tool, post-tool, pre-push, stop, session-end. Exits 0, except --client kiro, which exits 2 to deny a git push (and fails closed on an error during a push check) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli codewatch pre-commit`](#prism-cli-codewatch-pre-commit) | pre-commit hook: gitleaks scan of staged changes (blocks on a finding; installed by enable codewatch) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli codewatch pre-push`](#prism-cli-codewatch-pre-push) | pre-push hook: report-only code review of the branch diff (never blocks; installed by enable codewatch) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli codewatch report`](#prism-cli-codewatch-report) | Write a codewatch scan report (one pre-push review and its secret scans) as Markdown, HTML or JSON |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli codewatch review`](#prism-cli-codewatch-review) | Agent harness loop: review the changes an AI agent made (gitleaks first, then the AI review) and answer pass, fix or stop. Exit 0 pass, 3 fix, 4 stop, 1 error |
| [`prism-cli enable`](#prism-cli-enable) | Turn on a PRISM feature on this machine or repo: codewatch hooks, agent harness hooks, codeburn sync, Security Agent, the Kiro Crew app |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli enable claude-code`](#prism-cli-enable-claude-code) | Set Claude Code's status line to prism-cli statusline in your Claude Code user settings (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR respected), after a diff, a backup and your confirmation |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli enable codeburn`](#prism-cli-enable-codeburn) | Set up codeburn: local only (default), sync to your team's PRISM every 12h (--url), or the platform-team steps (--admin) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli enable codewatch`](#prism-cli-enable-codewatch) | Install codewatch git hooks: gitleaks pre-commit (blocks) and a report-only pre-push code review (kiro-cli or Claude Code). Turn them off in a repo with "git config prism.codewatch false" |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli enable agent-hooks`](#prism-cli-enable-agent-hooks) | Install the agent harness loop hooks (push check, opt-in finish check) for a coding client without a PRISM plugin: Kiro CLI V3 / IDE (.kiro/hooks/prism-harness.json) or Claude Code (.claude/settings.json hooks; skipped when the PRISM plugin is installed). Backs up, merges, and prints what it changed |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli enable kirocrew`](#prism-cli-enable-kirocrew) | Install or update the PRISM Kiro Crew app bundled with this prism-cli (a PRISM page, the PRISM MCP tools, a fix-findings skill and a daily digest) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli enable security`](#prism-cli-enable-security) | Set up AWS Security Agent: deploy only its stack (after a diff and your confirmation), then the application, the code review for this repo and its SSM pointer |
| [`prism-cli export`](#prism-cli-export) | Push local usage data to PRISM now |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli export otel`](#prism-cli-export-otel) | Push AI usage and commit attribution to the PRISM OTEL collector now (codeburn sync push, as the schedule runs it) |
| [`prism-cli git`](#prism-cli-git) | Claude Code session hook, and the retired AI-origin commit trailers |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli git claude-session-context`](#prism-cli-git-claude-session-context) | Claude Code SessionStart hook: capture the session id for AI-origin commit attribution (no jq required) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli git commit-trailers`](#prism-cli-git-commit-trailers) | [deprecated] Emit AI-origin commit trailers for the retired prepare-commit-msg hook (kept so already-installed hooks keep working) |
| [`prism-cli parse-code-tool`](#prism-cli-parse-code-tool) | Parse Kiro CLI and Kiro IDE sessions into codeburn-compatible token usage |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli parse-code-tool kiro-cli`](#prism-cli-parse-code-tool-kiro-cli) | Parse Kiro CLI session files and output token usage (codeburn-compatible JSON) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli parse-code-tool kiro-ide`](#prism-cli-parse-code-tool-kiro-ide) | Parse Kiro IDE session files and output token usage (codeburn-compatible JSON) |
| [`prism-cli security`](#prism-cli-security) | AWS Security Agent code reviews, threat models and pentests of this repo, and their results |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli security code-review`](#prism-cli-security-code-review) | Run an AWS Security Agent code review of this branch (or --full repo) now, wait for it and print the findings |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli security findings`](#prism-cli-security-findings) | List the findings of this repo's latest AWS Security Agent code review (or, with --pentest, its penetration test) and cache them for the dashboard (read-only) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli security pentest`](#prism-cli-security-pentest) | Deploy this repo's app into a temporary private VPC and run an AWS Security Agent penetration test against it |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli security threat-model`](#prism-cli-security-threat-model) | Run an AWS Security Agent threat model of this repo at HEAD, focused by design docs, wait for it and print the threats |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli security threats`](#prism-cli-security-threats) | List the threats of this repo's pending or latest (or --job) AWS Security Agent threat model and cache them for the dashboard (read-only) |
| [`prism-cli securityagent`](#prism-cli-securityagent) | [deprecated] securityagent setup is now prism-cli enable security |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli securityagent setup`](#prism-cli-securityagent-setup) | [deprecated] Alias for "prism-cli enable security" |
| [`prism-cli team`](#prism-cli-team) | Platform-team helpers: read the PRISM stack outputs, add developer telemetry accounts |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli team add-developer`](#prism-cli-team-add-developer) | AWS write: create a developer's telemetry account (Cognito user named by their email) after showing the plan and asking (needs cloudformation:DescribeStacks (unless --user-pool-id) and cognito-idp:AdminCreateUser) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli team info`](#prism-cli-team-info) | Read-only: print the PRISM stack's OtelCollectorUrl and OtelUserPoolId, and the line to send developers (needs cloudformation:DescribeStacks) |
| [`prism-cli workshop`](#prism-cli-workshop) | Workshop helpers: check prerequisites, deploy infrastructure, generate demo data, run the sample agent and pen test |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli workshop deploy-infra`](#prism-cli-workshop-deploy-infra) | Deploy workshop infrastructure via CDK (bootstraps if needed) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli workshop generate-demo-data`](#prism-cli-workshop-generate-demo-data) | Generate sample data for the PRISM dashboards (8 days of events + attribution) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli workshop perform-pen-test`](#prism-cli-workshop-perform-pen-test) | Deploy sample-app and run Security Agent pen test setup (Lambda + API Gateway + domain verification) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli workshop run-agent`](#prism-cli-workshop-run-agent) | Run the PRISM task assistant agent |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;[`prism-cli workshop verify-setup`](#prism-cli-workshop-verify-setup) | Verify environment prerequisites for the workshop |

## Deprecated commands

These still work and print a deprecation notice. Use the command each one names.

| Command | Status |
|---|---|
| `prism-cli bootstrapper install-git-hooks` | Alias for "prism-cli enable codewatch" (the prepare-commit-msg trailer hook is retired) |
| `prism-cli bootstrapper setup-otel-sync` | Alias for "prism-cli enable codeburn" |
| `prism-cli git commit-trailers` | Emit AI-origin commit trailers for the retired prepare-commit-msg hook (kept so already-installed hooks keep working) |
| `prism-cli securityagent setup` | Alias for "prism-cli enable security" |

## `prism-cli`

```text
Usage: prism-cli [options] [command]

PRISM D1 Velocity CLI tool

Options:
  -V, --version         output the version number
  -h, --help            display help for command

Commands:
  dashboard [options]   Local web dashboard (127.0.0.1 only): codewatch
                        results, codeburn usage, and a Setup page that runs
                        local setup steps. Read-only in AWS.
  mcp                   MCP server on stdio for Kiro, Claude Code and other MCP
                        clients: read-only codewatch findings and reports,
                        cached spend and the setup checklist, a static
                        dashboard snapshot file, the live dashboard on
                        127.0.0.1 as a child process, and prism_review, which
                        runs the harness review now and writes its result file.
                        The MCP server itself opens no port; it exits when
                        stdin closes, stopping that dashboard.
  statusline [options]  Claude Code status line: reads Claude Code's status
                        JSON on stdin and prints the latest codewatch review
                        counts, spend today and this month, and the session's
                        cost, lines, context and cache. Reads cached files
                        only; set it up with prism-cli enable claude-code.
  version [options]     Print the CLI version, check npm for a newer release,
                        and warn about other prism-cli copies on PATH
  assessment            Run the PRISM D1 Velocity assessment: scan a repo, or
                        run or deploy the assessment web app
  aws                   Connect an AWS profile, run read-only account checks
                        and turn them into a fix list
  bedrock-protection    Audit an AWS account, organization or repo for
                        LLMjacking exposure
  bootstrapper          Install PRISM CI workflows, the eval harness and the
                        coding agent, and set up CI OIDC roles
  codewatch             Git hook entry points and scan reports for the local
                        codewatch hooks, and the agent harness loop (review,
                        hook)
  enable                Turn on a PRISM feature on this machine or repo:
                        codewatch hooks, agent harness hooks, codeburn sync,
                        Security Agent, the Kiro Crew app
  export                Push local usage data to PRISM now
  git                   Claude Code session hook, and the retired AI-origin
                        commit trailers
  parse-code-tool       Parse Kiro CLI and Kiro IDE sessions into
                        codeburn-compatible token usage
  security              AWS Security Agent code reviews, threat models and
                        pentests of this repo, and their results
  securityagent         [deprecated] securityagent setup is now prism-cli
                        enable security
  team                  Platform-team helpers: read the PRISM stack outputs,
                        add developer telemetry accounts
  workshop              Workshop helpers: check prerequisites, deploy
                        infrastructure, generate demo data, run the sample
                        agent and pen test
  help [command]        display help for command
```

## `prism-cli dashboard`

Guide: [Local Dashboard](../USER_GUIDE.md#local-dashboard)

```text
Usage: prism-cli dashboard [options]

Local web dashboard (127.0.0.1 only): codewatch results, codeburn usage, and a
Setup page that runs local setup steps. Read-only in AWS.

Options:
  --json                 Print the dashboard data as JSON and exit (no server)
  --root <dir>           Where to look for git repos, 3 levels deep (default:
                         your home directory)
  --all                  [deprecated, no effect] every repo under --root is now
                         shown by default
  --port <n>             Port on 127.0.0.1 (default: a random free port)
  --no-open              Do not open a browser
  --snapshot <file>      Write the dashboard as one static HTML file (data
                         embedded, no server, no token, mode 0600) and exit
  --exit-on-stdin-close  Stop the server when stdin closes (prism-cli mcp uses
                         this so the dashboard ends with the session)
  --open                 With --snapshot: open the file in a browser when a
                         display is available
  --fresh                With --json: run the codeburn exports now instead of
                         using the usage cache (~/.prism/cache, 5 minutes)
  --timing               With --json: print how long each stage took to stderr
  -h, --help             display help for command
```

## `prism-cli mcp`

Guide: [MCP server](../USER_GUIDE.md#mcp-server-prism-cli-mcp)

```text
Usage: prism-cli mcp [options]

MCP server on stdio for Kiro, Claude Code and other MCP clients: read-only
codewatch findings and reports, cached spend and the setup checklist, a static
dashboard snapshot file, the live dashboard on 127.0.0.1 as a child process,
and prism_review, which runs the harness review now and writes its result file.
The MCP server itself opens no port; it exits when stdin closes, stopping that
dashboard.

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## `prism-cli statusline`

Guide: [Claude Code status line](../USER_GUIDE.md#claude-code-status-line)

```text
Usage: prism-cli statusline [options]

Claude Code status line: reads Claude Code's status JSON on stdin and prints
the latest codewatch review counts, spend today and this month, and the
session's cost, lines, context and cache. Reads cached files only; set it up
with prism-cli enable claude-code.

Options:
  --no-session  Print only the PRISM row, not the session row
  --json        Debug: print what it would show, and the files it read, as JSON
  -h, --help    display help for command
```

## `prism-cli assessment`

Guide: [Assessment Guide](../assessment/ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md#cli-commands)

```text
Usage: prism-cli assessment [options] [command]

Run the PRISM D1 Velocity assessment: scan a repo, or run or deploy the

Options:
```

### `prism-cli assessment deploy-cdk`

```text
Usage: prism-cli assessment deploy-cdk [options]

Deploy the assessment web app to AWS via CDK (ECS + Cognito + ALB)

Options:
  --hosted-zone <domain>   Route53 hosted zone domain (e.g. prism.example.com)
  --subdomain <name>       Subdomain for the app (default: "assessment")
  --certificate-arn <arn>  ACM certificate ARN (auto-created if omitted)
  --profile <name>         AWS CLI profile
  --region <region>        AWS region (default: "us-east-1")
  --destroy                Destroy the stack instead of deploying
  -h, --help               display help for command
```

```text
interview-agent

Options:

```

```text
Run the PRISM D1 Velocity scanner against a repository
```

## `prism-cli aws`

Guide: [AWS Account Advice](../USER_GUIDE.md#aws-account-advice-aws-connect-check-recommend)

```text
Usage: prism-cli aws [options] [command]

Connect an AWS profile, run read-only account checks and turn them into a fix
list

Options:
  -h, --help           display help for command

Commands:
  check [options]      Read-only AWS account checks: Bedrock protection, PRISM
                       setup, account baseline (results saved for aws recommend
                       and the dashboard)
  connect [options]    Choose and verify the AWS profile and region the other
                       AWS commands default to (read-only; stores no
                       credentials)
  recommend [options]  Turn the latest aws check result into a ranked fix list
                       (no AWS calls; --refresh runs aws check first)
  help [command]       display help for command
```

### `prism-cli aws check`

Guide: [aws check](../USER_GUIDE.md#aws-check)

```text
Usage: prism-cli aws check [options]

Read-only AWS account checks: Bedrock protection, PRISM setup, account baseline
(results saved for aws recommend and the dashboard)

Options:
  --profile <name>      AWS CLI profile (default: AWS_PROFILE or env
                        credentials, else the one saved by prism-cli aws
                        connect, else the default chain)
  --region <region>     AWS region (default: AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION,
                        the aws connect region, else the profile's region;
                        refuses when none is set)
  --section <name>      Run only this section, repeatable: bedrock,
                        prism-setup, baseline, startup-advisor (default: all)
  --fail-on <severity>  Exit 1 if any FAIL is at or above this severity
                        (CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|none; default none: report
                        only) (default: "none")
  --json                Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the report
  -h, --help            display help for command
```

### `prism-cli aws connect`

Guide: [aws connect](../USER_GUIDE.md#aws-connect)

```text
Usage: prism-cli aws connect [options]

Choose and verify the AWS profile and region the other AWS commands default to
(read-only; stores no credentials)

Options:
  --profile <name>   AWS CLI profile to save (default: choose from aws
                     configure list-profiles on a terminal)
  --region <region>  Region to save (default: AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION or
                     the profile's region; asked on a terminal)
  --repo             Save (or clear) a per-repo override in
                     .prism/aws.local.json instead of ~/.prism/aws.json
  --status           Show what is saved, where it comes from, and whether it
                     still validates
  --clear            Remove the saved connection (the user file, or the repo
                     file with --repo)
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

### `prism-cli aws recommend`

Guide: [aws recommend](../USER_GUIDE.md#aws-recommend)

```text
Usage: prism-cli aws recommend [options]

Turn the latest aws check result into a ranked fix list (no AWS calls;
--refresh runs aws check first)

Options:
  --profile <name>   AWS CLI profile (default: AWS_PROFILE or env credentials,
                     else the one saved by prism-cli aws connect, else the
                     default chain)
  --region <region>  AWS region (default: AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the
                     aws connect region, else the profile's region; refuses
                     when none is set)
  --account <id>     Account whose result to read (default: the aws connect
                     account, else the latest result)
  --refresh          Run prism-cli aws check first (read-only AWS calls)
  --json             Print the recommendations as JSON
  --markdown         Also write a Markdown report next to the result in
                     .prism/results/
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## `prism-cli bedrock-protection`

Guide: [Bedrock Protection Audit](../USER_GUIDE.md#bedrock-protection-audit)

```text
Usage: prism-cli bedrock-protection [options] [command]

Audit an AWS account, organization or repo for LLMjacking exposure

Options:
  -h, --help              display help for command

Commands:
  scan-account [options]  Audit the AWS account for LLMjacking exposure: IAM
                          credential hygiene plus Bedrock spend guardrails,
                          detection speed and invocation logging
  scan-org [options]      Audit an AWS Organization or specific OUs:
                          per-account IAM credential hygiene plus org-wide
                          Bedrock spend guardrails
  scan-repo [options]     Scan a git repository for credentials with gitleaks:
                          full history across all refs, working tree, commit
                          messages, and ignore-file hygiene
  help [command]          display help for command
```

### `prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-account`

```text
Usage: prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-account [options]

Audit the AWS account for LLMjacking exposure: IAM credential hygiene plus
Bedrock spend guardrails, detection speed and invocation logging

Options:
  --region <region>     Region for Bedrock, CloudWatch and Provisioned
                        Throughput checks (default: AWS_REGION,
                        AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the aws connect region, the
                        profile's region, else us-west-2)
  --profile <name>      AWS CLI profile to audit (default: AWS_PROFILE or env
                        credentials, else the one saved by prism-cli aws
                        connect, else the default chain)
  --max-key-age <days>  Flag active access keys older than this (default: "90")
  --unused-days <days>  Flag credentials idle longer than this (default: "90")
  --iam-only            Only run the IAM credential hygiene checks
  --bedrock-only        Only run the Bedrock spend guardrail and forensics
                        checks
  --json                Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the report
  --fail-on <severity>  Exit non-zero if any finding is at or above this
                        severity (CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|none) (default:
                        "none")
  -h, --help            display help for command
```

### `prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-org`

```text
Usage: prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-org [options]

Audit an AWS Organization or specific OUs: per-account IAM credential hygiene
plus org-wide Bedrock spend guardrails

Options:
  --ou <ids>                    Comma-separated OU ids to scope to (default:
                                the entire organization, recursing from every
                                root)
  --role-name <name>            Role to assume in each member account (default:
                                "OrganizationAccountAccessRole")
  --region <region>             Region for Bedrock, CloudWatch and Provisioned
                                Throughput checks (default: AWS_REGION,
                                AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the aws connect region, the
                                profile's region, else us-west-2)
  --profile <name>              AWS CLI profile to audit (default: AWS_PROFILE
                                or env credentials, else the one saved by
                                prism-cli aws connect, else the default chain)
  --max-accounts <n>            Stop after this many accounts (each costs ~10
                                AWS API calls) (default: "50")
  --session-duration <seconds>  AssumeRole session length (default: "3600")
  --max-key-age <days>          Flag active access keys older than this
                                (default: "90")
  --unused-days <days>          Flag credentials idle longer than this
                                (default: "90")
  --skip-bedrock                Skip the org-wide Bedrock spend guardrail
                                checks
  --skip-guardrails             Skip the SCP and AWS Config organization
                                guardrail checks
  --json                        Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the
                                report
  --fail-on <severity>          Exit non-zero if any finding is at or above
                                this severity (CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|none)
                                (default: "none")
  -h, --help                    display help for command
```

### `prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-repo`

```text
Usage: prism-cli bedrock-protection scan-repo [options]

Scan a git repository for credentials with gitleaks: full history across all
refs, working tree, commit messages, and ignore-file hygiene

Options:
  --repo <path>         Repository to scan (default: ".")
  --gitleaks <path>     Path to the gitleaks binary (default: $GITLEAKS_PATH,
                        then PATH)
  --skip-history        Skip the full-history scan (it is the slow one on a
                        large repo)
  --json                Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the report
  --fail-on <severity>  Exit non-zero if any finding is at or above this
                        severity (CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|none) (default:
                        "none")
  -h, --help            display help for command
```

## `prism-cli codewatch`

Guide: [Codewatch](../USER_GUIDE.md#codewatch-local-git-hooks)

```text
Usage: prism-cli codewatch [options] [command]

Git hook entry points and scan reports for the local codewatch hooks, and the
agent harness loop (review, hook)

Options:
  -h, --help          display help for command

Commands:
  hook [options]      Agent harness loop hook adapter: reads a coding client's
                      hook JSON on stdin and prints its decision. Clients:
                      claude, kiro. Events: claude session-start, pre-tool,
                      post-tool, stop, pre-push, bash-guard, session-end; kiro
                      session-start, pre-tool, post-tool, pre-push, stop,
                      session-end. Exits 0, except --client kiro, which exits 2
                      to deny a git push (and fails closed on an error during a
                      push check)
  pre-commit          pre-commit hook: gitleaks scan of staged changes (blocks
                      on a finding; installed by enable codewatch)
  pre-push [options]  pre-push hook: report-only code review of the branch diff
                      (never blocks; installed by enable codewatch)
  report [options]    Write a codewatch scan report (one pre-push review and
                      its secret scans) as Markdown, HTML or JSON
  review [options]    Agent harness loop: review the changes an AI agent made
                      (gitleaks first, then the AI review) and answer pass, fix
                      or stop. Exit 0 pass, 3 fix, 4 stop, 1 error
  help [command]      display help for command
```

### `prism-cli codewatch hook`

```text
Usage: prism-cli codewatch hook [options]

Agent harness loop hook adapter: reads a coding client's hook JSON on stdin and
prints its decision. Clients: claude, kiro. Events: claude session-start,
pre-tool, post-tool, stop, pre-push, bash-guard, session-end; kiro
session-start, pre-tool, post-tool, pre-push, stop, session-end. Exits 0,
except --client kiro, which exits 2 to deny a git push (and fails closed on an
error during a push check)

Options:
  --client <client>  Coding client: claude | kiro
  --event <event>    Hook event: session-start | pre-tool | post-tool | stop |
                     pre-push | bash-guard | session-end
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

### `prism-cli codewatch report`

Guide: [Scan Reports](../USER_GUIDE.md#scan-reports)

```text
Usage: prism-cli codewatch report [options]

Write a codewatch scan report (one pre-push review and its secret scans) as
Markdown, HTML or JSON

Options:
  --repo <path>     Repository (default: the current one)
  --id <result-id>  Result id (file name in .prism/results/ without .json)
  --commit <rev>    Report on the newest review whose pushed range includes
                    this commit (a sha, short sha, HEAD or branch)
  --format <fmt>    Output format: md | html | json (default: "md")
  --output <file>   Write to a file instead of stdout
  -h, --help        display help for command
```

### `prism-cli codewatch review`

```text
Usage: prism-cli codewatch review [options]

Agent harness loop: review the changes an AI agent made (gitleaks first, then
the AI review) and answer pass, fix or stop. Exit 0 pass, 3 fix, 4 stop, 1
error

Options:
  --working         Review the working tree (tracked and untracked) against the
                    session baseline (default with --session)
  --staged          Review the index against HEAD
  --since <ref>     Review <ref>...HEAD plus uncommitted changes (default: the
                    upstream, else the remote default branch)
  --session <id>    Use the baseline and round counter of this agent session
  --scope <scope>   Which findings count: new-lines | files | branch (default
                    new-lines with --session, else branch)
  --max-rounds <n>  Fix rounds before stop (default harness.max_rounds, 2;
                    ceiling 3)
  --timeout <s>     Per-attempt reviewer timeout in seconds (default
                    harness.timeout_seconds, 120)
  --no-review       gitleaks and the tamper check only, no AI review
  --json            Print the verdict JSON (schema prism.harness.verdict) on
                    stdout, nothing else
  -h, --help        display help for command
```

## `prism-cli enable`

```text
Usage: prism-cli enable [options] [command]

Turn on a PRISM feature on this machine or repo: codewatch hooks, agent harness
hooks, codeburn sync, Security Agent, the Kiro Crew app

Options:
  -h, --help             display help for command

Commands:
  claude-code [options]  Set Claude Code's status line to prism-cli statusline
                         in your Claude Code user settings (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
                         respected), after a diff, a backup and your
                         confirmation
  codeburn [options]     Set up codeburn: local only (default), sync to your
                         team's PRISM every 12h (--url), or the platform-team
                         steps (--admin)
  codewatch [options]    Install codewatch git hooks: gitleaks pre-commit
                         (blocks) and a report-only pre-push code review
                         (kiro-cli or Claude Code). Turn them off in a repo
                         with "git config prism.codewatch false"
  agent-hooks [options]  Install the agent harness loop hooks (push check,
                         opt-in finish check) for a coding client without a
                         PRISM plugin: Kiro CLI V3 / IDE
                         (.kiro/hooks/prism-harness.json) or Claude Code
                         (.claude/settings.json hooks; skipped when the PRISM
                         plugin is installed). Backs up, merges, and prints
                         what it changed
  kirocrew [options]     Install or update the PRISM Kiro Crew app bundled with
                         this prism-cli (a PRISM page, the PRISM MCP tools, a
                         fix-findings skill and a daily digest)
  security [options]     Set up AWS Security Agent: deploy only its stack
                         (after a diff and your confirmation), then the
                         application, the code review for this repo and its SSM
                         pointer
  help [command]         display help for command
```

```text
"git config prism.codewatch false"

  --reviewer <tool>  Team default reviewer: kiro | claude (skips detection)
```

## `prism-cli security`

```text
Usage: prism-cli security [options] [command]

AWS Security Agent code reviews, threat models and pentests of this repo, and
their results

Options:
  -h, --help              display help for command

Commands:
  code-review [options]   Run an AWS Security Agent code review of this branch
                          (or --full repo) now, wait for it and print the
                          findings
  findings [options]      List the findings of this repo's latest AWS Security
                          Agent code review (or, with --pentest, its
                          penetration test) and cache them for the dashboard
                          (read-only)
  pentest [options]       Deploy this repo's app into a temporary private VPC
                          and run an AWS Security Agent penetration test
                          against it
  threat-model [options]  Run an AWS Security Agent threat model of this repo
                          at HEAD, focused by design docs, wait for it and
                          print the threats
  threats [options]       List the threats of this repo's pending or latest (or
                          --job) AWS Security Agent threat model and cache them
                          for the dashboard (read-only)
  help [command]          display help for command
```

### `prism-cli security code-review`

Guide: [Running a Review](../USER_GUIDE.md#running-a-review-from-the-cli)

```text
Usage: prism-cli security code-review [options]

Run an AWS Security Agent code review of this branch (or --full repo) now, wait
for it and print the findings

Options:
  --profile <name>          AWS CLI profile (default: AWS_PROFILE or env
                            credentials, else the profile saved by prism-cli
                            aws connect, else the standard credential chain)
  --region <region>         AWS region (default: AWS_REGION,
                            AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the aws connect region, else
                            the profile's configured region)
  --path <dir>              The repository top level to work on (default: the
                            current directory, which must be the top level)
  --repo <host/owner/name>  Repo id (not a path) for the code review, as the CI
                            gate names it (default: from the origin remote)
  --full                    Review the whole repo at HEAD instead of the branch
                            diff
  --timeout <minutes>       How long to wait for the job (default: 30)
  --fail-on <level>         Exit 1 when any finding is at or above this level:
                            critical | high | medium | low
  --json                    Print only the final result JSON (progress goes to
                            stderr)
  --no-wait                 Start the job, print its id and exit
  -h, --help                display help for command
```

### `prism-cli security findings`

Guide: [Running a Review](../USER_GUIDE.md#running-a-review-from-the-cli)

```text
Usage: prism-cli security findings [options]

List the findings of this repo's latest AWS Security Agent code review (or,
with --pentest, its penetration test) and cache them for the dashboard
(read-only)

Options:
  --profile <name>           AWS CLI profile (default: AWS_PROFILE or env
                             credentials, else the profile saved by prism-cli
                             aws connect, else the standard credential chain)
  --region <region>          AWS region (default: AWS_REGION,
                             AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the aws connect region, else
                             the profile's configured region)
  --path <dir>               The repository top level to work on (default: the
                             current directory, which must be the top level)
  --repo <host/owner/name>   Repo id (not a path) for the code review, as the
                             CI gate names it (default: from the origin remote)
  --job <id>                 A specific code review job (default: the latest
                             for this repo)
  --latest                   The latest job for this repo (the default)
  --severity <level>         Show only findings at or above: critical | high |
                             medium | low
  --pentest [job]            Read the latest (or given) penetration-test job
                             instead of a code review
  --include-false-positives  With --pentest: show findings the agent rated
                             FALSE_POSITIVE confidence
  --wait                     If the job is still running, wait for it
  --timeout <minutes>        How long --wait waits (code review: 30; pentest:
                             360)
  --json                     Print only the result JSON
  -h, --help                 display help for command
```

### `prism-cli security pentest`

Guide: [Running a Penetration Test](../USER_GUIDE.md#running-a-penetration-test-from-the-cli)

```text
Usage: prism-cli security pentest [options]

Deploy this repo's app into a temporary private VPC and run an AWS Security
Agent penetration test against it

Options:
  --app-type <type>          How to build and deploy the app (default:
                             dockerfile; v1 ships only dockerfile)
  --path <dir>               The repository top level (default: the current
                             directory)
  --app-dir <dir>            Docker build context, relative to the repo root
                             (default: "path" in .prism/pentest.json, else .)
  --dockerfile <file>        Dockerfile, relative to the repo root (default:
                             "dockerfile" in .prism/pentest.json, else
                             <app-dir>/Dockerfile)
  --wait                     Wait for the job and print findings (default: do
                             not wait — a run takes hours)
  --timeout <minutes>        How long --wait waits (default: 360)
  --keep                     Do not tear the environment down after the job
                             (remove it later with --cleanup)
  --status                   Refresh and print the latest pentest job; tear
                             down once it has finished. No deploy
  --cleanup                  Tear down a prior run's environment now and exit.
                             No deploy
  --dry-run                  Show the plan, target and cost; deploy and start
                             nothing
  --yes                      Approve the deploy and the pentest without a
                             prompt (CI and other non-interactive use)
  --include-false-positives  Show findings the agent rated FALSE_POSITIVE
                             confidence (hidden by default)
  --fail-on <level>          Exit 1 on a non-false-positive finding at or above
                             this level: critical | high | medium | low
  --profile <name>           AWS CLI profile (default: AWS_PROFILE or env
                             credentials, else the profile saved by prism-cli
                             aws connect, else the standard credential chain)
  --region <region>          AWS region (default: AWS_REGION,
                             AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the aws connect region, else
                             the profile's configured region)
  -h, --help                 display help for command
```

## `prism-cli team`

Guide: [Step 5: Create Developer Accounts](../USER_GUIDE.md#step-5-create-developer-accounts)

```text
Usage: prism-cli team [options] [command]

Platform-team helpers: read the PRISM stack outputs, add developer telemetry
accounts

Options:
  -h, --help                       display help for command

Commands:
  add-developer [options] <email>  AWS write: create a developer's telemetry
                                   account (Cognito user named by their email)
                                   after showing the plan and asking (needs
                                   cloudformation:DescribeStacks (unless
                                   --user-pool-id) and
                                   cognito-idp:AdminCreateUser)
  info [options]                   Read-only: print the PRISM stack's
                                   OtelCollectorUrl and OtelUserPoolId, and the
                                   line to send developers (needs
                                   cloudformation:DescribeStacks)
  help [command]                   display help for command
```

### `prism-cli team add-developer`

```text
Usage: prism-cli team add-developer [options] <email>

AWS write: create a developer's telemetry account (Cognito user named by their
email) after showing the plan and asking (needs cloudformation:DescribeStacks
(unless --user-pool-id) and cognito-idp:AdminCreateUser)

Arguments:
  email                the developer's email; it is also the username

Options:
  --profile <name>     AWS CLI profile (default: AWS_PROFILE or env
                       credentials, else the one saved by prism-cli aws
                       connect, else the default chain)
  --region <region>    AWS region (default: AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the
                       aws connect region, else the profile's region; refuses
                       when none is set)
  --user-pool-id <id>  Cognito user pool (default: the PRISM stack's
                       OtelUserPoolId output)
  --yes                Create without the confirmation prompt (for scripts)
  --dry-run            Show the plan (account, region, pool, email); change
                       nothing
  -h, --help           display help for command
```

```text
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## `prism-cli workshop`

```text
Usage: prism-cli workshop [options] [command]

Workshop helpers: check prerequisites, deploy infrastructure, generate demo
data, run the sample agent and pen test

Options:
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Commands:
  deploy-infra [options]        Deploy workshop infrastructure via CDK
                                (bootstraps if needed)
  generate-demo-data [options]  Generate sample data for the PRISM dashboards
                                (8 days of events + attribution)
  perform-pen-test [options]    Deploy sample-app and run Security Agent pen
                                test setup (Lambda + API Gateway + domain
                                verification)
  run-agent [options]           Run the PRISM task assistant agent
  verify-setup [options]        Verify environment prerequisites for the
                                workshop
  help [command]                display help for command
```

```text
Usage: prism-cli workshop deploy-infra [options]

Deploy workshop infrastructure via CDK (bootstraps if needed)

Options:
  --require-approval <type>  CDK approval level (never, broadening, any-change)
                             (default: "never")

                             credentials)

```

### `prism-cli workshop generate-demo-data`

```text
Usage: prism-cli workshop generate-demo-data [options]

Generate sample data for the PRISM dashboards (8 days of events + attribution)

Options:
  --region <region>  AWS region (default: "us-west-2")
  --bus <name>       EventBridge bus name (default: "prism-d1-metrics")
  --team <id>        Team identifier (default: "demo-team")
  --repo <name>      Primary repository name (default: "prism-d1-sample-app")
  --table <name>     Attribution (AI usage) table name (default:
                     "prism-d1-ai-usage")
  --no-attribution   Emit events only; leave the attribution store untouched
  --purge-demo       Delete previously seeded attribution items and exit
  --force            Seed attribution even when the table already holds real
                     data
  --profile <name>   AWS CLI profile to audit (defaults to the ambient
                     credentials)
  -h, --help         display help for command
```
